evidence: The original code renames the record to its holder- name and only then calls filelock.Acquire, which opens O_CREATE|O_RDWR without O_EXCL, so a reader's exclusive probe in that gap can unlink it and the publisher recreates an empty held file. The agent's reason for declining lock-then-rename (on Windows, Go opens without FILE_SHARE_DELETE) is sound and was confirmed later in F20. But the replacement it shipped in bef3c2a (mint under holder-, hold, then fill) opened a held-but-empty window (F14/F15) and was replaced again in 486b606.
guidance_note: Before posting 'Fixed' on a concurrency race, list every interleaving of the new ordering against two or more concurrent readers, including a reader's O_CREATE probe recreating a name another reader just unlinked, and run the stress test under -race before replying.

evidence: The quoted 'e.g. snapshots restore, an init backlog adopt, or lifeboat recover' is the workspace lock's message, but the reproduction was against the commit lock, whose wrapCommitLockContention text is different. bef3c2a's CHANGELOG diff replaces it with the commit lock's message.
guidance_note: When a changelog quotes an error message as evidence, copy it from the code path the reproduction actually exercised, not from memory of a similar message.

evidence: This duplicates F1's rename-before-flock race; the agent posted the same diagnosis and the same Windows-based rejection of lock-then-rename. The secondary claim, that two readers can misreport a dead record while one is reaping it, belongs to the same class the agent later found with its own -race test (two sweepers manufacturing and retiring the same name).
guidance_note: When a reviewer describes a second-reader interleaving, put that exact interleaving into the stress test before choosing a new ordering.

evidence: HoldMirrorBeacon's contention branch built a new fmt.Errorf that dropped err, so the holder account never reached that message. bef3c2a appends ': %v' with err and keeps the sentinel unpropagated, which is one of the two fixes the reviewer offered.
guidance_note: When adding text that rides an error to every wrapper, grep every errors.Is(err, sentinel) branch for a wrapper that builds a fresh error instead of wrapping.

evidence: This is the third copy of F1's rename-then-lock race and got the same reply. Declining lock-then-rename was right because of Windows sharing modes; the fix chosen instead was itself defective (see F14/F15).

A staging-* file left by a publisher killed before the rename was never swept, because readLockHolders scans only holder- entries. bef3c2a deleted the staging prefix. The 486b606 redo brought the same leak back as minting-* and later private-* (F24), so the 'removed by construction' claim held only for one commit.
guidance_note: When a later commit replaces the design an earlier 'fixed by construction' reply relied on, re-check and correct every thread that cited that design.

evidence: With the holder dir unreadable, the account printed 'a process that left no record' next to 'holder records unreadable', asserting something the read could not establish. The fallback now depends on whether problems is empty (unnamedHolder(problems)), as the reviewer proposed.
guidance_note: When a fallback message asserts a fact, make sure it is chosen only on the branch where the read that establishes that fact succeeded.

evidence: The CHANGELOG's claim that the account reaches 'every lock message' was false because of HoldMirrorBeacon. The reviewer asked for the claim to be narrowed; the agent made it true in code (the F4 fix), which is the better resolution.

This is the fourth copy of F1's race, including the O_CREATE-without-O_TRUNC resurrection detail, and got the same reply. The reviewer's 'flock follows the open file description' fix is POSIX-only, and the agent was right to reject it for Windows.
This duplicates F6's staging-* leak and got the same reply and fix in bef3c2a (staging prefix deleted). The leak came back with the minting-/private- prefix in 486b606 (F24).

The reviewer suggested ': %w', which would propagate the ErrWorkspaceBusy sentinel and contradicts the reviewer's own 'even though the sentinel itself is deliberately not propagated'. The agent used %v and pinned errors.Is false in TestBeaconContentionNamesTheSquatter.

The mirror beacon's budget is 20x50ms (~950ms), shorter than the 2s grace, so the comment's 'briefest budget is ~5s' was false. The agent took the comment-correction option the reviewer offered and argued well against a sub-second grace.
guidance_note: When a comment justifies a constant with a superlative ('the briefest budget here'), compute every peer budget in the package before writing it.

evidence: This flag is a false positive: bef3c2a does not touch commit_lock.go, so the filepath.Dir(lockPath) derivation in acquireCommitLockAtPath dates from the original commit. The agent threaded the storage dir by changing LockCommitPath to take databasePath (5877638), but it missed the main_signal_test.go call site (F26).
guidance_note: When adding a storageDir parameter to every lock wrapper, derive it from the same helper everywhere in the first commit rather than inverting one lock's path.

evidence: bef3c2a (the F1 fix) made a held, zero-byte file visible under the swept holder- name between Acquire and fillHeldRecord. The original write-then-rename never showed readers an empty live record. 486b606 (pushed before the reply) moved the fill behind a private minting- name, so 'already fixed' is accurate.
guidance_note: When reordering create/lock/write steps to close a race, state for each step what a concurrent reader sees under the swept name; a held-but-empty state is a new reader-visible state.

evidence: This is the same held-but-empty window as F14, which bef3c2a introduced. The agent also correctly rejected the reviewer's re-read-after-probe idea, because on Windows the exclusive probe would lock out the read. 486b606 had already removed the window.

This flag is a false positive: bef3c2a's workspace_lock.go diff touches only HoldMirrorBeacon, and the non-deferred stopAnnouncing() in acquireStoreLock is from the original commit. A panic in filelock.Acquire with context.Background would strand the reporter goroutine. The fix is defer announceLockWait(...)().
guidance_note: When a function starts a goroutine and returns its stop func, defer the stop at the call site.

evidence: The commit-lock wrap was only tested with a bare sentinel, so dropping %w would have left the suite green. The gap dates from the original PR, not bef3c2a. TestCommitContentionNamesTheHolder was added and mutation-checked against both regressions the reviewer named.
guidance_note: When a PR claims a property for 'every wrapper', add one end-to-end contention test per wrapper in the original PR.

evidence: bef3c2a (F1 fix) rewrote doc.go to describe 'the bounded budget a publisher spends waiting that probe out'. 486b606, the redo of that fix, removed the retry budget but left doc.go unchanged. The reviewer's grep for lockHolderRetryAttempts finding nothing confirms the drift.
guidance_note: When a redo deletes a mechanism, grep the repo for every prose description of it that the previous commit added (here doc.go) and update them in the same commit.

evidence: This is the same doc.go sentence as F18. The bounded-wait mechanism it describes was added in bef3c2a and deleted in 486b606, while the shipped mint acquire uses maxAttempts 1, delay 0.

486b606 (the second attempt at F1's fix) locks a minting- file and then calls os.Rename while still holding it, which is the same Windows ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION the agent had used in round 0 to reject the reviewer's fix. The agent confirmed it in the Go source and switched to os.Link instead of going back to minting under holder-, which is already known to race.
guidance_note: When a fix was chosen to satisfy a stated platform constraint, check every later redo of that fix against the same constraint before pushing.

evidence: This duplicates F20 (rename while holding the lock, on Windows). Both suggested alternatives are rejected correctly: minting under holder- reopens the race, and filelock does not pass FILE_SHARE_DELETE. Fixed with os.Link in 67a2d8d.
This is the third finding on the doc.go 'bounded budget' sentence, which bef3c2a added and 486b606 made stale. It was fixed in c02bd57.

486b606 switched record names from CreateTemp (O_EXCL) to pid+seq published by os.Rename, which silently replaces an existing name. A reused pid could then overwrite a dead un-swept record, so a reader would pair the stale payload with the new holder. The agent's choice of os.Link, which fails with EEXIST, makes the collision loud rather than less likely, which is stronger than the reviewer's random suffix.
guidance_note: When replacing an O_EXCL-created name with a deterministic one, check whether the publish primitive can replace an existing file, and use a non-replacing one (link/O_EXCL).

evidence: 486b606 (the F1 redo) brought back the staging-style leak (minting-*) that the F6/F10 replies said was gone by construction, and those replies were never corrected. The agent withdrew the false claim and accepted the leak as a documented cost. It correctly declined an age sweep: probing private names would contend with the publisher's maxAttempts-1 acquire.
guidance_note: When a redo reintroduces a shape an earlier thread called 'fixed by construction', post a correction on that thread in the same push.

evidence: mintHeldRecord fills before it links, so a kill after the fill leaves a complete private record, not a 'byte-less' one. 67a2d8d, the F24 fix, rewrote this comment and called it accurate but kept 'byte-less'. The fix drops the emptiness claim and stages a filled record in the test.
guidance_note: When rewriting a comment that describes what a crash leaves behind, walk each step of the function and state what is on disk if the process dies after that step.

evidence: 5877638, the F13 fix, changed LockCommitPath's parameter from lock path to database path, both typed string. cmd/lit/main_signal_test.go:116 kept passing the lock path and still works only because commitLockPathForDolt is idempotent. The agent admitted its grep for CommitLockPath never matched LockCommitPath, and swept every call site this time.
guidance_note: When changing what a same-typed parameter means, grep the exact function name across the whole module (including cmd/ and tests) before pushing, or make the change a type change so the compiler finds the call sites.

evidence: bf070df's CHANGELOG diff fixed the second clause ('a file nothing ever opens') but left 'leaves an empty file that no sweep collects' in the same sentence. The agent admits this: 'the claim lived in four places and I fixed three, then one.'
guidance_note: When correcting a false claim, grep for every phrasing of it (empty file, byte-less, names nobody) in all files before pushing, not just the sites the reviewer cited.

narrative: Round 0 found a real rename-then-lock race in holder-record publishing, reported four times. The agent rightly rejected the reviewer's lock-then-rename fix for Windows, but its first replacement (bef3c2a) opened a held-but-empty window and failed its own -race stress test. The second replacement (486b606) brought back the rename-while-locked Windows bug the agent had itself cited, a pid-reuse silent replace, the staging leak, and a stale doc.go sentence. Every finding in rounds 2-4 traces back to the F1 fix being redesigned twice, plus two incomplete sweeps (a LockCommitPath call site and a CHANGELOG clause). The round-5 push hit the review cap and went unreviewed.
guidance_observations: The agent replied 'Fixed in bef3c2a' to the race threads before its stress test had shaken out the design, and when 486b606 replaced that design the earlier 'fixed by construction' replies (F6/F10) were left uncorrected until a reviewer caught it.

A constraint the agent stated in its own reply (no rename of a held file on Windows) was violated by its next commit, so constraints cited in review replies should be re-checked against every later commit on the same code.

Two incomplete-sweep findings (F26, F27) came from grepping the cited line or a near-anagram name instead of every phrasing of the changed fact; the agent only swept the whole class after being caught twice.
